title: Carry active-Agent self-review over the foreground stream

requirement.summary: Extend the vendor-neutral agentgov dev --stream connection with a strict two-stage active-Agent self-review exchange: the Coding Agent requests a medium-risk review after resolved alignment, AgentGov returns the exact normalized materialization request, the same Adapter returns small observation drafts, and AgentGov returns the accepted digest-bound advisory result.

objective.rationale: The self-review callback is executable inside the Python Adapter but cannot yet be driven by a real foreground Coding Agent connection; a strict request/draft exchange is the smallest portable installation boundary.

goal: Add strict start, draft, and response contracts plus an in-memory stream session that prepares and completes active-Agent self-review on the same resolved alignment and Coding Agent identity, then integrate it with agentgov dev --stream.
non_goals: Do not add a vendor SDK, model endpoint, API key, account configuration, network call, hosted service, background Agent, or independent Reviewer integration.
Do not assume that an adapter_id identifies Codex, Claude Code, an IDE, a model, or an assurance level; portable Provider capability remains explicit.
Do not accept raw prompts, raw answers, transcripts, assistant responses, source content, credentials, model prompts, absolute paths, host-selected observation IDs, or authority claims.
Do not auto-start review before the human alignment decision is resolved, accept low/high risk through this medium-risk path, or let the Agent select a high-risk fallback choice.
Do not persist review state across process restart, write repository/runtime state, or mutate the completed alignment dialogue.
Do not change stable 0.2.1, immutable v0.3.0rc1, release metadata, workflows, consumer repositories, or external systems.
acceptance_signals: Strict vendor-neutral active-agent-self-review-start and active-agent-self-review-draft input contracts exclude raw/private content, carry denied authority, and bind the adapter, resolved dialogue, active-host Provider, medium risk, allowed evidence, and exact pending request.

A strict active-agent-self-review-stream-response reports either one materialization_required request with normalized ephemeral context or one completed accepted run; impossible field/status combinations fail.

The in-memory session starts only against the exact current resolved AlignmentStreamResponse, accepts only the same Coding Agent adapter, emits one deterministic request binding, and never calls a model itself.

A valid draft from the same adapter completes through the existing active-Agent materializer result builder, preserves self_review assurance and advisory-only denied authority, and cannot supply observation IDs, route, Provider binding, or result identity.

Unknown contracts/fields, duplicate IDs, out-of-order start/draft, unresolved or stale alignment, adapter drift, request digest drift, wrong risk/provider, empty/duplicate/malformed/out-of-allow-list observations, sensitive/local content, context mutation, retry races, and authority drift fail before stream state advances; a valid retry remains possible where safe.

agentgov dev --stream dispatches lifecycle, alignment, self-review start, and self-review draft records on one foreground connection, preserves exact line numbers and fail-fast behavior, and returns pure JSONL in JSON mode.

Codex and Claude Code active-host fixtures complete the same four-record alignment-to-review journey without vendor branches in Core; no user-authored JSON is claimed as an ordinary product requirement because host Adapters own these records.
No implementation code performs network I/O, loads credentials, starts an Agent, selects a model, writes repository/runtime state, applies a human choice, or persists review context across restart.

Affected source-of-truth, public documentation, schemas, and tests accurately distinguish the implemented live transport from still-open native host callback installation and independent Reviewer integration.
Focused/full tests, current-task, scope, repository, schemas, compile, and diff validation pass.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_self_review_transport tests.test_active_agent_self_review tests.test_alignment_transport tests.test_reference_alignment_adapter tests.test_semantic_review tests.test_coding_agent_transport tests.test_agent_skills tests.test_task_contract tests.test_user_documentation tests.test_portfolio_docs -v

items: A stateful stream could bind a draft to the wrong alignment, Provider, adapter, or request after an invalid record or retry.
Embedding normalized review context in a response could accidentally expose raw conversation, host-local paths, credentials, or undeclared source content.
Host-authored drafts could try to supply result identity, overstate independence, invent evidence, or gain authority.
Adding transport records can increase protocol weight unless they reuse existing contracts and remain invisible to ordinary user input.

stop_conditions: Stop if a review request can be produced before the exact human alignment resolution or for low/high risk.
Stop if a draft can cross adapter, dialogue, Provider, route, or request bindings, or if invalid input advances session state.
Stop if raw/private content, host-selected result identity, false independence, silent downgrade, or any project/external authority enters the stream contracts.
Stop if ordinary users must author stream JSON, enter a new confirmation, or configure a second model/account.
Stop if the transport writes repository/runtime state or survives foreground process restart.
Stop before any external model call, Provider setup, network access, external write, Git write, publication, release, deployment, or consumer mutation.

decision.rationale: The user reviewed and accepted the completed live active-Agent self-review transport on 2026-08-06, then explicitly authorized the recommended native host Adapter proof as the next requirement.
